Back in 2011, I had to put up with this on PS3, which had a Memory Leak issue, causing the game to slow down abruptly after many hours of gameplay. Nowadays, any decent PC can run this game smooth as butter. I envy people who never played an RPG as ambitious as this before. Look past the dated graphics and you will find a true gem of a game, giving tremendous freedom to the player. It really is Bethesda's Magnum Opus, in my opinion.

This is truly one of the best games I've ever played. I can lose myself in there for hours and hours.

It's beautiful (but doesn't require a super-computer), the music is amazing, the world is immersive, if you want to you can mod it until it breaks (I know people are raging about Creation Club but you can ignore it, there's plenty of free mods), you can shout at things (FUS RO DAH!) - what are you waiting for?

The year was 2011 - a young gimpyboy89 was excited to play Skyrim on release day after having been years late to the world of Oblivion. Gimpygirl90 suggested that we get a pizza and dive into the new entry in the Elder Scrolls series, and for the next hundred hours I ignored college classes and explored every mountain/cave/ruin I could find.

Now 11 years later I decided to take a trip down memory lane. Some things have changed, gimpygirl90 is now gimpywife90 and we have three gimpykids, but Skyrim still holds all the magic and wonder that it did 11 years ago. This game is truly a high water mark for the industry and if by some horrible course of events you've never played it yet, you owe it to yourself to experience the grandure of this epic game.

This, for me, is one of the BEST RPGs! Been adventuring in Skyrim all over again from another Steam account to this current account, but with another character type. There's just so much to do in this game!

If you don't like the base game mechanics, there are A LOT of mods to fix those issues, or fan-made patches, or just more content(more spells,armors,weapons etc.) .
I personally like the story, and if you don't like, then you can always 1. change parts of the main quest 2. mod so it never even happened. or 3. Download new more interesting quests.
Right now i have about 500h on SE and +100h on Oldrim, so i can confidently say that is IS a good game, maybe not a rpg, but close, and i personally have, and will still enjoy this game, i hope this was helpful. (but creation club is bs)

On of the best games I ever played. It has an amazing modding community. In short this game is for everyone. Its a Bethesda game using a literal 100 year engine but its still amazing none of the less. This was the very first video game I ever played, So it does get old after a while. The mechanics of the game are go do this get rewarded. Its endless of hours of fun with mods. The lore of the Elder Scrolls is amazing, and Skyrim added so much, they re-release this game on EVERY console to ever exist, soon they will put it on a toaster probably. Don't get me wrong, its a great game. But do they really gotta release it on every console? It is also set in medieval times so no guns unless you mod them into the game. So basically there is something for everyone. So I give it a 6/10, it is indeed a game I love and a ton of other people love but next re-release they should give it better graphics, better mechanics, and better other things. This game is riddled with bugs due to their 100 year old engine. But like I said mods can fix those! But I am rating the base game not the mods.

Its a LOT more stable than old Skyrim and it can handle lot of fps draining visual mods without much fps loss in weaker rigs IF the ini is tweaked right. There are some really satisfying things I wish to point out:
1. Dragon skeletons are solid. You can no longer walk through them.
2. It can handle lot of NPC spawns without fps loss
3. Some NPC behaviors have been made better for example Ulfberth War-Bear does not wear his armor constantly
4. Tweakable Actor, Object, Grass, Item Fade options IN-GAME. And yeah Alt-Tabbing too.

And yeah now that the SKSE team is working on with SKSE64 its really going to be a worthy successor for 2011 Skyrim! :)

It's the same exact pseudo-RPG like the original with some sprinkles added to the lighting. I could tell it was the same exact game seeing as how that every result I came up with when I searched up the bugs & glitches I've experienced were all results for the original game. Since mods will sort of fix the game and make it look better than either version & that most mods are compatible with both, there's not really a good reason to get this version unless they remove the original from the store for whatever possibly suspicious reason or if you've received it for free by having the original + all of its DLC by the time that offer was valid. With buying the original you at least get a choice in what you do or don't want included regarding DLC for a lower price.
